scientific_goal: Determine whether greater nonlinear capacity and multiscale raw-state history can whiten held-out 0p10 one-step innovations, then determine whether short-horizon multistep fine-tuning can retain that gain while restoring stable autonomous rollout moments.
scientific_constraints: Tune and select only on validation repetitions 13 and 14; keep test repetitions 15 and 16 locked.

Use the saved 5 percent training-increment trim, rank-20 shared POD coordinates, 50 Hz high-pass spatial mean, native-lag velocity state, full diffusion, and diagonal damped-residual drift in every fresh matched arm.
Run the declared one-step history and capacity arms before adaptive tuning.
Separate history from capacity: compare history-1 and longer-history models at 128x128 before attributing a gain to either change.
Judge innovation whitening using both median and maximum validation ACF at lags 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 256, and 512; moving correlation into a longer tail is failure.
Treat validation NLL, innovation mean/covariance calibration, innovation ACF/PSD, rollout survival, energy, POD moments, and rollout PSD as separate evidence.
Do not promote a model solely for lower validation NLL or lower median ACF if leading-coordinate maximum ACF remains large.
Use 5000-step validation screens before any 50000-step confirmation.

After the one-step arms, apply multistep training only as a fine-tune of the best supported architecture. Start with horizons 2 and 5; test horizons 2, 5, 10, and 20 only if the short-horizon fine-tune is finite and preserves the innovation improvement.
Interpret rollout PSD against the process retained by the saved 5 percent training trim; do not optimize generated/untrimmed mid-frequency power toward one.
Prefer the smallest history stencil and network that materially improve innovation whitening while preserving stable rollout moments.
advisor_guidance: The stable memory-free parent has good 50000-step moments but colored validation innovations: whitened median absolute ACF is about 0.243, 0.331, and 0.165 at lags 1, 2, and 5, with maximum values about 0.906, 0.920, and 0.812. Existing multistep-trained raw-history models modestly reduced selected ACF values but badly inflated autonomous energy: history 1,2,5 with a 128x128 network reached about 4.24 times trimmed-reference energy, while history 1,2,5,10,20,50 with a 64x64 network reached about 6.72 times. Therefore first use matched one-step arms to determine whether history and capacity genuinely improve held-out conditional innovations. If a one-step architecture improves both median and maximum ACF without displacing correlation into lags 20 through 512, fine-tune that exact architecture with multistep horizons 2 and 5. Reject NLL-only improvements and screen rollout stability cheaply before confirmation. A longer candidate with offsets 100 and 150 is allowed only if the up-to-50-frame arms improve short-lag ACF but leave the leading-coordinate persistent tail unresolved.

seed_runs.hypothesis: The existing history-1 short-multistep model is the stable rollout and innovation baseline.
The existing sparse up-to-50-frame history model records the prior ACF improvement and rollout-amplitude failure.

initial_trials.hypothesis: A 128x128 one-step history-1 model separates the effects of one-step training and increased capacity from added history.
initial_trials.expected_observation: This control may lower validation NLL, but should not substantially whiten the leading-coordinate innovations if missing history is the main limitation.

initial_trials.hypothesis: Sparse multiscale history through 50 frames supplies missing predictive state without the optimization burden of every intermediate frame.
initial_trials.expected_observation: Relative to the matched history-1 control, both median and maximum validation innovation ACF decrease at short lags and the long-lag tail does not increase.

initial_trials.hypothesis: Dense access to the first ten frames plus offsets 20 and 50 resolves the sharp short-lag innovation structure better than a sparse stencil at matched capacity.
initial_trials.expected_observation: Lag-1-through-lag-10 innovation ACF improves beyond the sparse-50 arm without worsening calibration or creating a persistent tail.

initial_trials.hypothesis: The dense-short multiscale history requires greater nonlinear capacity to extract a predictive latent state rather than treating its information as diffusion.
initial_trials.expected_observation: Relative to the matched 128x128 history arm, validation innovation ACF and conditional-mean skill improve materially without worse covariance calibration or immediate rollout instability.
